data.title: Oil Falls As Iran Talks Raise Hopes Of Strait Of Hormuz Reopening
data.description:
Oil prices slipped on Thursday as progress in Iran-Oman talks raised hopes of a potential US-Iran peace deal that could eventually reopen the Strait of Hormuz, while fresh US inventory data added pressure to prices.

Brent crude futures fell 37 US cents or 0.5% to US$79.08 a barrel by 0024 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate declined 53 US cents or 0.7% to US$74.69. Brent had edged higher in the previous session while WTI finished slightly lower, according to Reuters.

Nomura Securities economist Yuki Takashima said selling pressure emerged after reports that the Iran-Oman talks were making progress, with prices returning to levels seen when the US and Iran reached an interim peace agreement on June 17.

A proposed deal could give Tehran control over ships entering the Gulf through the Strait of Hormuz, according to Iranian and regional sources cited by Reuters.

However, the US has not commented on the proposal and officials have previously opposed any arrangement that would give Iran control over access to the key energy shipping route.

Concerns over wider regional disruption also remain. Iran-aligned Houthis claimed attacks on two Saudi oil tankers, while Takashima said the risk of further attacks on Red Sea shipping was limiting optimism over an end to regional shipping disruptions.

Separately, US crude inventories rose by 2.5 million barrels to 407 million barrels in the week ended July 31, against analysts’ expectations for a 1.5 million-barrel draw, according to the Energy Information Administration.

data.title: HSIF Eyes 26,750 As RHB Sees Bullish Momentum Returning
data.description:
Hang Seng Index Futures (HSIF) could resume its upward movement after rebounding 76 points in the latest session, with RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) retaining its positive trading bias and long position.

The HSIF closed at 25,910 points after opening at 25,818 points and briefly falling to an intraday low of 25,698 points. It then reversed higher to reach 25,990 points, ending near the session high with a bullish candlestick that erased the previous session’s losses.

RHB said the fresh bullish candlestick and a rising Relative Strength Index above the 50% mark point to improving momentum. The index is also trading firmly above its 20-day and 50-day simple moving average lines, keeping the broader trend tilted towards the bulls.

“If the HSIF sustains above the 20-day SMA line, it is likely to move higher towards the 26,750 pts resistance,” RHB said.

The research house therefore recommended traders maintain the long position initiated at 24,657 points based on the July 15 close. It placed the stop-loss threshold at 23,500 points.

The HSIF’s immediate support is at 24,200 points, followed by 23,500 points, while resistance is seen at 26,000 points and then 26,750 points.

The bullish view comes despite weakness in the evening session, when the index fell 236 points to last trade at 25,674 points.

data.title: US Stocks Continue To Rise After Record Rally
data.description:
US stocks rose modestly on Wednesday after a searing rally, as investors weighed earnings from SpaceX and AMD and President Trump’s comments that a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz could happen as early as Wednesday.

The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite rose 0.4%. The S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average climbed 0.6% after the indexes closed at record highs

A rise in Asian markets overnight lifted global markets as investors assessed earnings and cheered diplomatic efforts for another peace deal between the US and Iran — no matter how fragile. South Korea’s KOSPI index led gains, rising almost 4%.

SpaceX didn’t receive the Wall Street welcome it was looking for in its first report as a public company. Shares of the Elon Musk-led company dropped 12% after its AI spending overshadowed a second quarter earnings beat. SpaceX stock faces additional pressure this week when 20% of shares will be unlocked for trading.

data.title: Wall Street Splits As Dow Rallies While Tech Stumbles
data.description:
The Dow Jones Industrial Average closed at a record high on Wednesday as hopes for progress towards a peace deal involving Iran helped support sentiment, although a sell-off in SpaceX and Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) shares pulled the Nasdaq lower.

The Dow rose 263.18 points, or 0.49%, to 54,349.06 while the S&P 500 slipped 13 points, or 0.17%, to 7,723.52. The Nasdaq Composite fell 221.55 points, or 0.83%, to 26,363.44, ending a four-session winning streak.

Markets have been buoyed by hopes of progress towards resolving the conflict with Iran, which has also pushed oil prices and US Treasury yields lower. The resulting easing in inflation concerns has reduced expectations of a Federal Reserve rate hike in September.

“It’s just a straight rocket shot that we’ve gone up, we didn’t even take a breath,” said Kenny Polcari, chief market strategist at Slatestone Wealth in Jupiter, Florida.

“It’s progress, but the market’s just going, we’re not going to give it to you this time until we actually see the progress, because how many times have we been jerked around over the last four months?”

SpaceX was among the biggest drags on the Nasdaq, with shares plunging 13.6% after the Elon Musk-led company reported its first earnings since going public.

Revenue nearly doubled while operating losses narrowed, helped by growth in its Starlink satellite communications and artificial intelligence businesses. However, investors were concerned about the scale of its spending on AI infrastructure, including data centres.

The stock could also face further pressure with its post-IPO lock-up period set to expire from Thursday.

AMD shares also fell 7% despite the chipmaker forecasting quarterly revenue above Wall Street expectations on strong demand for AI-related products. Investors appeared to be looking for clearer evidence that heavy AI infrastructure spending will translate into faster growth.

The Dow, meanwhile, received support from a 4.6% jump in Amgen after the drugmaker reported a 9% increase in second-quarter sales. Eli Lilly rose 4.9% after raising its full-year revenue forecast, helping the S&P 500 healthcare sector gain 1.3%.

Disney also contributed to the Dow’s gains, with its shares rising 3.6% after the entertainment company beat third-quarter profit expectations.

On the economic front, US private payroll growth slowed in July, according to the ADP national employment report, ahead of the government’s closely watched non-farm payrolls report due on Friday.

The Institute for Supply Management’s non-manufacturing purchasing managers’ index edged up to 54.1 in July from 54.0 in June, although it came in below economists’ forecast of 54.5. A reading above 50 still indicates expansion.

Investors remain focused on inflation and the Federal Reserve’s next move, with the market now pricing a 54.9% chance of a rate hike at the September meeting, down from 58.3% a week earlier.

Minneapolis Fed President Neel Kashkari said in an interview with CNBC that he believed it was time to begin slowly raising interest rates, while Federal Reserve Board Governor Lisa Cook and San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly were also scheduled to speak later in the day.

data.title: Bursa Malaysia Slips At Midday As AI Jitters Spur Profit-Taking

On the upside, Malaysian Pacific Industries Bhd led the gainers as the counter rose 70 sen to RM47.64, UWC Bhd gained 28 sen to RM6.76, while Theta Edge Bhd and ViTrox Corporation Bhd advanced 14 sen each to 69 sen and RM9.24 respectively.

data.title: Asian Stocks Retreat As Tech Rally Cools, Iran Talks Stay In Focus
data.description:
Asian shares retreated on Thursday as technology stocks pulled back after an AI-driven rally, while investors kept an eye on developments surrounding a potential Iran peace deal and the upcoming US jobs report.

MSCI’s broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan fell 0.69%, led by a 3.64% slide in South Korean shares and a 1.57% decline in Japan’s Nikkei. Samsung Electronics dropped 2.44%, while SK Hynix fell 6.95%. In Tokyo, Kioxia plunged 9.61% and Tokyo Electron declined 4.61%.

The pullback followed a weaker Wall Street session, with the Nasdaq ending a multi-day winning streak after investors remained cautious over lofty expectations for technology companies. Advanced Micro Devices fell despite beating analysts’ estimates, while concerns also emerged over the scale of data centre investment.

Oil prices remained relatively steady as markets assessed prospects for a deal involving Iran and Oman that could help reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Brent crude slipped 0.18% to US$79.31 a barrel while US West Texas Intermediate fell 0.35% to US$74.96.

Commonwealth Bank of Australia senior geo-economics analyst Madison Cartwright said a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz could be reached by early September, although he remained sceptical that an agreement was imminent.

Meanwhile, investors are turning towards Friday’s US non-farm payrolls report after ADP data showed private employers added just 44,000 jobs in July, below expectations. Futures markets now price a 54% chance of a Federal Reserve rate hike in September, down from 58% a day earlier.

Reuters

data.title: Dollar Lingers Near Six-Week Low, Yen Gives Up Ground
data.description:
The US dollar remained near a six-week low while the Japanese yen eased on Thursday as traders awaited further developments on a proposed US-Iran deal and Friday’s US jobs report for clues on the Federal Reserve’s next interest rate move.

The yen was 0.1% weaker at 157.88 per US dollar, giving back some of the gains following Japan’s recent intervention. It had strengthened to 155.20 on Monday but remains well above its multi-decade low of almost 164 reached in July.

The dollar index, which measures the US currency against six major peers, edged 0.1% higher to 99.76 after hitting a six-week low on Monday.

The euro was steady at US$1.1544 while sterling slipped 0.1% to US$1.3454. The Australian dollar fell 0.2% to US$0.7039 while the New Zealand dollar was also down 0.2% at US$0.5873.

Markets remained focused on developments around the Strait of Hormuz after a proposed deal between Iran and Oman was reported to potentially give Tehran control over inbound traffic through the strategic waterway.

There was no immediate US comment on the proposal, while President Donald Trump has said a deal to reopen the strait was imminent. US officials have repeatedly said Washington would not accept Iranian control over access to the key energy shipping route.

Brent crude was steady at around US$79.50 a barrel, close to levels last seen when the US and Iran reached an interim peace agreement in June.

Investors are now turning towards Friday’s US non-farm payrolls report, which could provide further clues on the Fed’s interest rate path after the central bank left rates unchanged last month.

A Reuters poll expects US employers to have added 80,000 jobs in July, up from 57,000 in June, while the unemployment rate is forecast to remain at 4.2%.

A stronger jobs reading could support the dollar by strengthening expectations of a September rate hike, while a weaker report could reinforce expectations that the Fed will keep rates unchanged.

data.title: Stock Today: Heineken Malaysia Falls 6% As Weak Results Weigh On Shares
data.description:
Heineken Malaysia Bhd shares fell nearly 6% in late morning trading on Thursday after weaker-than-expected second-quarter earnings prompted Hong Leong Investment Bank (HLIB) to cut its earnings forecasts and target price for the brewer.

As at 11.11am, Heineken Malaysia had fallen RM1.12 or 5.86% to RM17.98, with 1.59 million shares changing hands. The stock opened at RM19.00 and traded between an intraday high of RM19.02 and a low of RM17.92.

The decline came after the company reported second-quarter core profit after tax and minority interests of RM48.4 million, down 53.1% quarter-on-quarter and 41.7% year-on-year. First-half core earnings fell 26.3% year-on-year to RM151.7 million, coming in below both HLIB and consensus expectations.

HLIB attributed the weaker performance to subdued consumer sentiment and Heineken Malaysia’s deliberate reduction of ex-brewery sales initiatives as it seeks to keep distributor inventories closer to underlying demand.

The research house subsequently cut its FY2026, FY2027 and FY2028 earnings forecasts by 16.5%, 8.1% and 8.0% respectively, while lowering its target price to RM25.65 from RM28.07. It maintained a Buy call.

Despite the near-term pressure, HLIB sees potential upside from the planned transition to an import-based supply model by Asia Pacific Breweries (Singapore), which could add around 240,000 hectolitres of annual volume to Malaysia if 80% of Singapore’s volume is allocated to the country.

data.title: Stock Picks: 99 Speed Mart And Gamuda
data.description:

Following the breakout, RHB Research expects 99 Speed Mart to move towards the next resistance at RM3.85, followed by RM4. However, a fall below the RM3.50 support level would invalidate the bullish setup and signal a return to a correction phase.

Meanwhile, Gamuda is also seen extending its upward momentum after breaking above the RM4.40 resistance level.

RHB Research said the breakout points to strong bullish momentum, with the counter expected to head towards RM4.60 before potentially testing RM4.75.

On the downside, a breach of the RM4.25 support level would negate the bullish setup and trigger a correction phase.

data.title: Ringgit Opens Firmer As Soft US Data Weighs On Dollar
data.description:
The ringgit opened slightly higher against the US dollar on Thursday as weaker-than-expected US economic data weighed on the greenback and improved market sentiment.

At 8am, the local currency was quoted at 4.0905/0960 against the US dollar, compared with Wednesday’s close of 4.0920/0960.

Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said softer US data had pushed the US Dollar Index (DXY) down 0.18% to 99.676.

The US Automatic Data Processing (ADP) Nonfarm Employment Change came in at 44,000 in July, below the consensus estimate of 68,000 and down from 95,000 in June. Meanwhile, the US Institute for Supply Management’s non-manufacturing index stood at 54.1 in July, slightly below the 54.5 consensus estimate.

Mohd Afzanizam also noted that Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook had indicated support for an interest rate hike if inflation remained persistently high.

At the same time, the potential reopening of the Strait of Hormuz has kept Brent crude below US$80 a barrel, with Mohd Afzanizam expecting the US dollar-ringgit pair to trade between RM4.07 and RM4.09 today.

Quintex Intel global strategist Stephen Innes said the broader US dollar was slightly weaker in early trade, although risk sentiment had softened as investors waited for final details of a potential West Asia peace deal.

Markets are also entering the 48-hour window before the US non-farm payrolls report, prompting traders to rebalance risk and reduce exposure, which could keep the ringgit within a relatively narrow range in early trading.

Against other major currencies, the ringgit was mostly lower at the open. It weakened against the Japanese yen to 2.5942/5978 from 2.5940/5967 and slipped against the euro to 4.7266/7329 from 4.7222/7268.

However, it strengthened against the British pound to 5.5087/5161 from 5.5107/5161.

Against regional currencies, the ringgit fell against the Singapore dollar to 3.1932/1978 from 3.1916/1950 and weakened against the Thai baht to 12.3655/3881 from 12.3216/3381.

It edged higher against the Indonesian rupiah to 228.0/228.5 from 228.1/228.5 and was unchanged against the Philippine peso at 6.73/6.74.

data.title: Stock Today: SkyeChip Dips 0.33% Despite AI Chip Growth Prospects
data.description:
SkyeChip Bhd shares edged lower on Thursday as investors weighed the semiconductor designer’s growth prospects against its relatively high valuation, with the stock trading at RM3.05 as of 4.03pm.

The technology counter fell RM0.01 or 0.33% from its previous close of RM3.06. It opened at RM3.06 and moved between an intraday high of RM3.11 and a low of RM3.03, with 61,681 lots changing hands.

The stock’s performance comes after CIMB Securities highlighted SkyeChip’s positioning to benefit from growing global demand for AI semiconductors and next-generation computing technologies.

The research house said SkyeChip’s silicon intellectual property and custom application-specific integrated circuit design capabilities give it exposure to areas including high-bandwidth memory interfaces, Network-on-Chip architectures and die-to-die interface technology.

SkyeChip generates revenue mainly through licensing its intellectual property, alongside engineering and design fees from customised ASIC projects.

CIMB Securities also pointed to the company’s expanding ecosystem partnerships, including access to Advanced Semiconductor Engineering, one of the world’s largest outsourced semiconductor assembly and test providers. The partnership could support SkyeChip’s work in advanced packaging as the industry increasingly adopts chiplet architectures.

The company is also involved with JEDEC, the global microelectronics standards body, giving it a role in the development of specifications for memory technologies including LPDDR and HBM.

Despite the growth opportunities, valuation remains a consideration for investors. CIMB Securities said SkyeChip was trading at about 65 times calendar year 2027 earnings, based on Bloomberg consensus estimates, with the premium valuation supported by expectations of 32% earnings growth in CY2027.

As of Thursday’s close, SkyeChip remained just above the RM3 level, with buying volume at 2,446 lots against selling volume of 881 lots.

data.title: Stock Today: MR DIY Falls 1.95% As Investors Await 2Q Results

The shares were down three sen from their previous close of RM1.54, with the last done price also sitting below the opening level.

Investors will be looking for signs of consumer spending strength and the resilience of Malaysia’s retail sector, alongside updates on sales momentum, store expansion, profitability and management’s outlook for the rest of the financial year.

The upcoming results will also provide a fresh read on how the group performed during the April-to-June period as it navigates changing consumer spending patterns and broader economic conditions.

data.title: Gold Rallies To US$4,175, RHB Sticks With Short Call
data.description:
Gold climbed for a third straight session on Wednesday, hitting a one-month high as a softer US dollar and falling oil prices supported demand for the precious metal while investors awaited fresh US jobs data for clues on the Federal Reserve’s next interest-rate move.

Spot gold rose 2.4% to US$4,175.53 an ounce by 0640 GMT, its highest level since July 7, while US gold futures gained 2% to US$4,235.30.

The dollar remained subdued, making gold and other greenback-priced commodities more attractive to holders of other currencies. At the same time, crude oil extended its decline following steep falls in the previous two sessions.

Lower oil prices have eased concerns over inflation and the prospect of higher interest rates, with markets now pricing in a 59% probability of a Federal Reserve rate hike at its September 15-16 meeting, down from 67% a day earlier.

The retreat in oil came as Qatar said mediators were making progress towards ending the US-Iran war, although Tehran has denied US President Donald Trump’s assertion that talks are already underway.

“Gold’s relation with oil is still intact as oil prices have a tremendous impact on the global economy in terms of inflationary pressure. If we get a very clear roadmap to further de-escalation in tensions, gold prices could move higher,” said Kelvin Wong, senior market analyst at OANDA.

Investors are now looking to the ADP employment report due later on Wednesday and the July payrolls report on Friday for further clues on the Fed’s policy direction.

Gold’s latest rally has also brought it closer to a key technical level identified by RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research), which continues to maintain a bearish view on COMEX gold.

COMEX gold rose US$61.60 on Tuesday to close at US$4,121.90 after trading between US$4,068.70 and US$4,132.60. RHB Research said the precious metal remains in a see-saw formation and has yet to break through its immediate resistance.

The research house said the 50-day simple moving average remains a key overhead resistance level and is expected to hold as long as gold stays below US$4,200.

“For now, we hold on to the negative trading bias,” RHB Research said.

RHB Research advised traders to retain short positions initiated at US$4,605.70, with a stop-loss threshold at US$4,200. It identified US$4,000 as the first support level, followed by US$3,850, while resistance is seen at US$4,200 and then US$4,400.

A close above US$4,200, however, would negate RHB Research’s bearish technical setup.

Elsewhere in precious metals, spot silver jumped 3.8% to US$61.76 an ounce while platinum gained 2.6% to US$1,779.25 after earlier reaching its highest level since mid-June. Palladium also rose 2.6% to US$1,389.15 after touching a two-month high.

data.title: Gold Hits Seven-Week High As Hormuz Hopes Lift Bullion
data.description:
Gold prices climbed for a fourth straight session on Thursday, reaching their highest level in seven weeks as a weaker US dollar and renewed hopes of a reopening of the Strait of Hormuz supported demand for the precious metal.

Spot gold rose 0.2% to US$4,254.98 an ounce by 6.36am GMT, after earlier touching its highest level since June 18. US gold futures also gained 0.2% to US$4,312.80.

The move came after bullion posted its biggest one-day gain since February on Wednesday, with investors weighing the prospects of a diplomatic breakthrough between Iran and the US that could ease disruption around the key energy shipping route.

A proposed deal between Iran and Oman could give Tehran control over ships entering the Gulf through the Strait of Hormuz, according to Iranian and regional sources cited by Reuters. The possibility of an agreement has also weighed on oil prices, while easing expectations for higher interest rates have provided further support for gold.

Market expectations for a September US rate hike have eased to 55%, from 67% two days earlier, while the dollar index remained under pressure. A weaker US currency typically makes dollar-priced gold cheaper for holders of other currencies.

Investors are now looking towards Friday’s US non-farm payrolls report for further clues on the Federal Reserve’s interest rate path. A weaker jobs reading could further support gold by strengthening expectations for lower rates, while a stronger-than-expected report could put short-term pressure on bullion.

RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) has also turned bullish on COMEX gold after the commodity broke above the US$4,200 resistance level.

The research house said gold surged past the level on Wednesday to close at US$4,273.30, forming a long bullish candlestick and signalling stronger upward momentum.

RHB Research has initiated a long position at US$4,273.30, with a stop-loss at US$3,950. It sees the commodity potentially moving towards US$4,400, with support at US$4,100 followed by US$3,950. Resistance is seen at US$4,400 and US$4,650.

Elsewhere, spot silver fell 0.5% to US$61.78 an ounce, while platinum gained 0.8% to US$1,755.18 after touching its highest level since June. Palladium rose 0.8% to US$1,748.08 for its third consecutive session.

data.title: Bursa Extends Rally As FBM KLCI Jumps 15.5 Points To 1,748
data.description:
Bursa Malaysia extended its upward run on Aug 5, with the benchmark index climbing 15.51 points as investor sentiment improved on hopes of easing tensions in West Asia.

The FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) rose 0.9% to close at 1,748.17, after trading between 1,732.68 and 1,750.41.

The broader market also strengthened with the FBM Emas gained 93.19 points to 12,902.51, the FBM Shariah advanced 110.12 points to 12,732.63, while the FBM 70 added 66.46 points to 18,277.96.

Among index heavyweights, Maybank rose four sen to RM10.82 and Tenaga Nasional Bhd gained 16 sen to RM14.66.

Public Bank Bhd slipped one sen to RM5.27, CIMB Group Holdings Bhd fell two sen to RM8.01 and IHH Healthcare Bhd declined 11 sen to RM8.32.

Zetrix AI Bhd was the most actively traded counter, falling 4.5 sen to 69 sen with 113.15 million shares changing hand. Inari Amerton Bhd jumped 20 sen to RM2.41 with 69.94 million shares traded, Genetec Technology Bhd gained 5.5 sen to 38 sen on 68.34 million shares and NationGate Holdings Bhd advanced seven sen to RM1.36 on 64.09 million shares exchanged hand, while EG Industries Bhd dropped 10 sen to RM1.70 with 43.61 million shares.

Turnover surged to 3.89 billion units worth RM3.8 billion from 2.8 billion units valued at RM2.81 billion on Aug 4.
